essence: Pool the fly's T4/T5 direction-selective outputs inside each track's fovea in a radial-opponent pattern, the way LPLC2 does: four dendritic arms each collect outward motion in one cardinal lobula-plate layer and are inhibited by inward motion. An LC4-like fast-loom readout can be added alongside. The project's fovea is a square crop around the predicted box (side 2*max(w,h), min 64 px), rescaled to the eye every frame. So a residual expansion or contraction measures the scale-prediction error (dw/dh), not raw approach. Localized or asymmetric edge motion across part of the fovea marks an occluder entering or the object leaving. Proposed uses: (a) a correction or uncertainty for w,h in the XYWH Kalman state; (b) an occlusion-onset feature for q_alive and the lost-track buffer; (c) an approach / time-to-contact cue.

relevance: Occlusion is the biggest live target in plan §5 item 4: 70.8% of objects are occluded, the gap to clean objects is 27.34 pp, 51% of it runs through underestimated confidence and 49% through blindness or box inaccuracy. The second half is what a box-scale/occlusion cue could address. Box-scale dynamics clearly matter: the independent w,h Kalman state (XYWHByteTrack) raised val7 HOTA 52.437 -> 54.573 (+4.1%) and cut IDSw 573 -> 526 (-8.2%) (FLYVIS_VIDEO_RATE_EXPERIMENT_REPORT.md). Re-association after loss is the weak spot of q_match (lost stratum AP 0.386 vs 0.944 tracked, event_heads_v1), and q_alive and the lost-track buffer are line-B components. Registry: H11 (functions where the fly is native: looming via LPLC2 is explicitly listed in M4), H10 (fovea resolution and scale), and goal 3's dw/dh heads, which were never tested with a fly readout (H1 tested only dx,dy direction).
novelty_overlap: LPLC2/looming models are numerous, and all target collision detection: Zhou et al. 2022; Gu et al. 2024; OppLoD 2023; Liu & Fu 2025 (multi-target localization); Schubert et al. 2025 (automotive, event camera). Connectome work (Nature 2025) already maps the T4/T5 -> LPLC2 synaptic gradients. In MOT, scale and occlusion cues come from box height (Hybrid-SORT 2024), pseudo-depth ordering (SparseTrack, PD-SORT 2025) and depth plus camera pose (DepthMOT 2024). The search found no work using an LPLC2-like readout of connectome-constrained FlyVis as a box-scale or occlusion cue inside an MOT tracker, but that absence is not proof of novelty. cannot_claim: first looming detector from a fly model; LPLC2 or LC4 modelled from the connectome (FlyVis lacks them, so the pooling is our design unless FlyWire LPLC2 synapse weights are imported); novelty of occlusion reasoning in MOT; superiority over the box-derived scale rate already in the Kalman state unless that control is beaten.
author_results: Klapoetke 2017: LPLC2 responds selectively to loom (radial outward motion centred in its receptive field), not to translation or wide-field motion; calcium imaging, electrophysiology and escape behaviour; no video benchmark. Zhou 2022: anatomically constrained shallow networks trained only to detect collisions reproduce LPLC2 tuning on many stimuli without neural data; synthetic stimuli. Gu 2024: T4/T5 motion times T2/T3 feature multiplication; training data 2,886 and test 972 samples from 241 panoramic HDR images (1D pixel-line stimuli); the combined pathway gives a 10-25% increase in estimation accuracy (R^2) under dynamic backgrounds and at least 50% better speed estimation with fast background motion; generalizes to AirSim 3D and a real UAV obstacle-avoidance demo. Liu & Fu 2025: synthetic 33 Hz stimuli (100x100, 320x240) and 44 real UAV sequences; qualitative evaluation with no accuracy metrics; attention fields reportedly form within about 7 frames [uncertain: the latency figure is inconsistent in the text]; the LGMD2 baseline wrongly responds to bright receding objects; no code. Schubert 2025: simulated driving-accident scenarios with event-camera data; detects colliding vehicles up to 1.3 s before collision. SparseTrack: DanceTrack test HOTA 55.5, IDF1 58.3, AssA 39.1 with IoU-only matching. PD-SORT/DepthMOT report gains on MOT17/DanceTrack/VisDrone/UAVDT [uncertain: exact numbers not retrieved]. None of the bio-inspired works uses BDD100K or real 30 Hz dashcam MOT; cameras are mostly static or UAV-mounted.
measured_level: Bio-inspired works: neuron-like response or collision-warning timing on synthetic or UAV clips (R^2, time before collision). MOT depth/scale works: HOTA/IDF1 after TrackEval. No work measures an LPLC2 readout at pair (AP) or HOTA level in MOT.
matched_control: External: Gu 2024 ablates pathways (motion-only T4/T5, feature-only T2/T3, combined), which is a component control, not a same-information control. Liu & Fu compare against LGMD2 and a single LPLC2. None uses a shuffled-graph null. Controls required here: (1) box-derived scale velocity from the XYWH Kalman state plus detection-score dynamics (geometry-only head); (2) divergence of DIS flow in the same crop (same information, non-fly; the dis_quarter cache is too sparse inside small boxes, so compute DIS on full-resolution crops); (3) input-only: the same radial-opponent pooling over temporal differences or an EMD on the 721-facet eye input after the lamina front-end; (4) FlyVis with the degree- and sign-preserving shuffled connectome (fly_connectome_null_v1 infrastructure); (5) a structure control: identical T4/T5 pooling with the arm-to-layer assignment rotated (non-radial), to test whether radial opponency itself matters.
conditions_breakdown: External: static vs dynamic background (Gu 2024), object size and speed (Liu & Fu); no night, overexposure or occlusion breakdown. Needed here: BDD100K 'occluded'/'truncated' box attributes at labelled frames, dark vs bright videos, box size bins, and fast-approach / cut-in cases.
cost_here: Per-frame, per-track T4/T5 fields inside the fovea are not stored. runs/fly_signatures keeps only first/last-5-step averages (34 types x 19 macrocolumns), and runs/train_cache/*/fovea_flow.npz keeps only the mean residual delta, magnitude, pred_box, dis_box and out_box. Stage 0 (CPU, cached data only): define targets as (a) the relative w,h error of the Kalman prediction against the matched detection (from pred_box/out_box in fovea_flow.npz) and (b) occlusion onset from BDD 'occluded' attributes at 5 Hz. Fit a geometry head and a DIS-crop-divergence head (DIS about 7 ms/frame on CPU). Hours of CPU. Stage 1 (GPU): patch EyeBank to also save per step the divergence and curl of the decoded residual flow (the (2, hexals) field is already in memory) plus four radial-opponent T4a-d/T5a-d arm sums. Re-run the fovea pass with the lamina retina on val7 + 70 dev/test videos: 25-89 ms/frame; the comparable signature pass took about 4 h wall for 147 videos with 7 processes, so about 2 h wall here, launched with Idle priority per plan §9. Heads and per-video bootstrap: CPU minutes. Go to HOTA only if AP beats all controls: dw/dh correction or q_alive feature in XYWHByteTrack on cached detections, TrackEval dev/test about 1 h CPU.
expected_effect: Low. H1 already showed no usable directional position correction from residual fovea flow, and constant velocity at the 33 ms step is near the prediction ceiling. Smooth scale change behaves similarly: a car at 20 m closing at 10 m/s changes scale by about 1.7% per 30 Hz frame, a sub-pixel radial shift at the edge of a 64-px eye and below T4/T5 spatial resolution. So a dw/dh correction is expected to be about 0 except for abrupt cut-ins. For occlusion onset, an occluder produces strong translating edge motion. The fly's motion magnitude carried that information, but DIS mismatch carried it more strongly (H2: +0.02 vs +0.10 AP), and overall the fly added only +0.006 AP over its own input (+0.010 at night). Expected q_alive gain over geometry+DIS: at most +0.005 AP, likely with a CI through zero [uncertain]. Expected HOTA change: about 0. The only plausible positive niche is partial occlusion and cut-ins at night, where DIS degrades and the lamina front-end helps the fly (+0.009 AP night, H2 stage B).
risks: (1) FlyVis lacks LPLC2/LC4, so the pooling is handmade and interpretation is weak without the structure and shuffle controls. (2) By construction, fovea normalization to the predicted box removes the expansion signal whenever prediction is good. crop_box also shifts crops inside the frame and clips the side at borders, which creates spurious expansion; mask or model this. min_side = 64 hides expansion for small objects. (3) Labels at 5 Hz give coarse occlusion-onset timing, and the BDD 'occluded' attribute is binary per box. (4) The eye input is grayscale; night glare and headlight blooming mimic expansion. (5) Project rules: detector frozen (satisfied); one condition changed per comparison; no gain claims without per-video bootstrap CI; short-run signs not transferred; GPU re-runs only via Start-Process with Idle priority; a negative result is recorded as completed_negative, not as novelty.
attribution: Ours: the LPLC2-like radial-opponent readout of frozen FlyVis T4/T5 activity inside a tracker-driven fovea, its use as a box-scale (dw/dh) correction or uncertainty and as an occlusion-onset feature for q_alive/buffer in XYWHByteTrack, and the matched controls. Borrowed and cited: the LPLC2 concept and radial motion opponency (Klapoetke et al. 2017); the anatomically constrained loom model (Zhou et al. 2022); motion-times-feature multiplication (Gu et al. 2024); ensemble/attention localization (Liu & Fu 2025); FlyWire T4/T5 -> LPLC2 connectivity (Nature 2025) if used; FlyVis (Lappalainen et al. 2024); XYWH state (BoT-SORT) and pseudo-depth occlusion ideas (SparseTrack, PD-SORT).
